correctness.rationale: Exact convex automorphism averaging covers arbitrary symmetric feasible matrices. All invariant matrices satisfy two row sums and are parametrized by x in [0,min(1,1/r)]. The full eigenbasis has eigenvalues 1, -(1-x)/(p-1) (multiplicity p-1), -(1-rx)/(q-1) (multiplicity q-1), 1-(1+r)x, and 0 (multiplicity p(a-1)+q(b-1)). The intersection points x_A=p/[p+(p-1)r], x_B=q/[q-1+qr], and the feasible interval caps prove the unique invariant optimum and exact four regimes for every p,q>=2,a,b>=1. The separate complete-matrix rational verifier passed 576512 assertions. Numerical grids are supplementary, not an infinite proof.
risks: Claim is only for real symmetric stationary-uniform zero-diagonal transition matrices; full-matrix uniqueness and nonreversible optimality are unproved.

value.rationale: The zero-holding requirement is a natural hard constraint on a transition mechanism that must move each step. The result completely solves a four-parameter family rather than calculating a small instance or routine numerical SDP, and identifies two exact edge-class deletion thresholds pa=b and a=qb and a third spectral obstruction switch at a=b. It proves that the optimum is scale invariant under uniform blow-up and that balancing the two part sizes uniquely minimizes the optimum SLEM for fixed p,q.
risks: No finite-horizon total-variation optimality is implied by minimizing the asymptotic SLEM.
